segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After saying these things, Jesus went out with his disciples across the Kidron Valley, where there was a garden, which he and his disciples entered.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Judas, who was handing him over, also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with his disciples.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Judas took the cohort, along with officers from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, and came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who are you looking for?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am he.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Judas, who was handing him over, was standing with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am he,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: they drew back and fell to the ground.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he asked them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who are you looking for?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Jesus the Nazarene.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these men go.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was to fulfill the word he had spoken:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Of those you have given me, I have not lost a single one.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus said to Peter,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Put the sword into its sheath. The cup the Father has given me—am I not to drink it?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the cohort and its commander and the officers of the Jewish leaders arrested Jesus and bound him

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and led him first to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish leaders that it was better for one man to die for the people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he went with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the slave girl who kept the door said to Peter,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You aren’t also one of this man’s disciples, are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I am not.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the slaves and the officers had made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were standing there warming themselves. Peter too was with them, standing and warming himself.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews come together, and I said nothing in secret.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Look, they know what I said.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he said this, one of the officers standing by gave Jesus a slap, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is that how you answer the high priest?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If I spoke wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You aren’t also one of his disciples, are you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He denied it and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I am not.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the high priest’s slaves, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Peter denied it again, and at once a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They themselves did not enter the headquarters, so that they would not be defiled but could eat the Passover.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Pilate went out to them and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What charge do you bring against this man?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “If this man were not doing wrong, we would not have handed him over to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Pilate said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Jewish leaders said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We are not permitted to put anyone to death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This was to fulfill the word Jesus had spoken, indicating what kind of death he was going to die.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Pilate went back into the headquarters, summoned Jesus, and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you the king of the Jews?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I am not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my officers would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jewish leaders. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Pilate said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “So then, you are a king?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I have come into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pilate said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What is truth?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Having said this, he went out again to the Jewish leaders and said to them,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I find no basis for a charge against him.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But you have a custom that I release one person to you at the Passover. So do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they shouted back,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Not this man, but Barabbas!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Barabbas was a bandit.

notes.note: The Greek verb is the ordinary word for transferring someone into another’s custody, and John uses the same word in this chapter for what the leaders do to Jesus before Pilate (verses 30, 35, 36). Most English versions say “betray” when Judas is the subject, which names the treachery the context supplies but hides the chain of handings-over. Some scholars defend “betray” as a legitimate contextual sense; the standard lexicons give “hand over” as the basic meaning.

notes.traditional: a band of men; a detachment of soldiers
notes.note: The word is the regular Greek term for a Roman cohort, on paper about six hundred men, though it could be used of a smaller unit, and its commander in verse 12 bears the title of a Roman tribune. John thus pictures Roman troops from the Jerusalem garrison alongside the temple officers. How many soldiers were actually present is not stated.

The Greek is simply “I am,” which is the normal way to say “That’s me” but is also the phrase John’s Jesus uses in an absolute sense that echoes God’s self-declaration in the Greek Scriptures (as at John 8:58). The arresting party’s falling to the ground in verse 6 suggests John intends the second meaning to be heard behind the first. English cannot carry both at once; the ordinary sense is given in the text.

The Greek word denotes a person owned by another, not a hired employee, and first-century readers would have understood Malchus as part of the high priest’s household property. Older English versions soften this to “servant”; several modern versions use “slave” here.

The Greek word is the ordinary one for “Jews,” and it is rendered that way in verses 20, 33, 35 and 39. In verses 12, 14, 31, 36 and 38, however, John uses it for the Jerusalem authorities who arrest and accuse Jesus, not for the Jewish people as a whole—Jesus, his disciples and the crowds are all Jews. Scholars are divided on how best to render John’s usage; some prefer “Judeans” throughout, others keep “Jews” everywhere.

The questioner here is Annas, since Jesus is sent on to Caiaphas only in verse 24. Annas had held the office earlier and had been deposed by the Romans, but he remained the head of the leading priestly family and evidently kept the title in common usage. Caiaphas, his son-in-law, was the officiating high priest.

The Greek borrows the Latin word praetorium, the official residence of a Roman governor, here Pilate’s base while in Jerusalem. Many versions keep the Latin term; it is translated here because the word means nothing to most modern readers. Its exact location in Jerusalem is disputed.

Entering a Gentile’s residence was held to make a person ritually unclean and so unable to share in the festival meal. In John’s account the Passover meal still lies ahead on the morning of the trial, whereas the other three Gospels present the Last Supper as a Passover meal. How the two chronologies relate is a long-standing and unresolved question.

notes.phrase: We are not permitted to put anyone to death
notes.traditional: It is not lawful for us to put any man to death
notes.note: Under Roman rule in Judea the power to execute appears to have been reserved to the governor, though the extent of this restriction is debated by historians. John sees a deeper point in verse 32: a Roman execution meant crucifixion, which matches Jesus’s earlier saying about being “lifted up” (John 12:32–33).

The same Greek word in the plural is usually translated “Gentiles,” meaning the non-Jewish peoples. Here, in the singular, it refers to the Jewish people as a nation, and Pilate uses it to distance himself from what he treats as an internal affair.

The Greek preposition expresses source or origin, and the closing clause of the verse restates the point as “not from here.” The traditional “of this world” can suggest that the kingdom has nothing to do with the world; the Greek says that its origin and authority do not come from the world. Several modern versions also read “from.”

Jesus uses the same word that John has used throughout the chapter for the officers of the chief priests who arrested him (verses 3, 12, 18, 22). Most versions switch to “servants” or “followers” here, which hides the echo: the leaders have their officers, and if Jesus’s kingship were of the same kind, his would be fighting too.

notes.phrase: You say that I am a king
notes.traditional: Thou sayest that I am a king
notes.note: The reply can be taken as a noncommittal “That is your word for it,” as an affirmation (“You are right to say that I am a king”), or, with different punctuation, as “You say so; because I am a king, for this I was born.” The text keeps the literal wording, which neither denies the title nor accepts it on Pilate’s terms. Most commentators see a qualified affirmation.

The Greek word denotes an armed, violent outlaw such as a brigand or highwayman, not a thief who steals by stealth. It was also applied to insurgents, and Mark and Luke connect Barabbas with an uprising, so some versions render it “rebel” or “revolutionary” here; that reading is possible but not certain. “Bandit” keeps the violence and outlawry without deciding the question.

candidates.reason: Used for temple police, court attendants, synagogue attendants and ministers of the word across the Gospels, Acts and Paul; versions vary between officer, guard, attendant, servant and minister, and John 18:36 plays on the repetition.
The slave/servant choice recurs throughout the New Testament and affects parables, household scenes and Paul’s self-descriptions; it needs one policy.
Occurs in all the Passion narratives, Acts 23:35 and Philippians 1:13, where versions vary between Praetorium, headquarters, palace and imperial guard.
Appears across the Gospels and Acts alongside Ναζαρηνός; translators vary between “of Nazareth,” “the Nazarene” and “the Nazorean,” and the choice should be uniform.
The Roman military unit recurs in the Passion narratives and Acts (10:1, 21:31, 27:1), rendered variously as cohort, band, detachment, regiment or battalion.
